global_rules.contract: Each diagnostic wrong option maps to a valid misconception ID; the correct option misconception is blank.
Wrong options are plausible for a learner but definitively wrong in the stated context.
Balance length, style, tense, register and naturalness across options.
Near-rule distractors are allowed/encouraged for hard items when they remain unambiguous.
Do not use spelling/typo-only noise as a substitute for a grammar misconception.
No two options may be semantically equivalent under the stated context.
Full and option-level explanations must not contradict the keyed answer or misconception mapping.
Avoid systematic correct-position and stylistic answer cues.
Distractors must remain within the Stage 6 lesson/subtopic/type compatibility contract.
Flag weak distractors heuristically when selection rate is <5% with N>=100; Stage 27 owns final calibrated thresholds.
Do not reuse a fixed distractor set mechanically across unrelated stems.

option_level_contract.traceability: selected wrong option -> misconception_id -> subtopic -> weakness/review
